claim: The fire that burned through Puerto Patriada and the Andean towns of El Hoyo and Epuyén in Argentina's Chubut province started at about 3pm on January 5, 2026. In a release dated January 7, the Fiscalía de la Circunscripción de Lago Puelo — the provincial prosecutors' office for the area — reported that a specialist fire examiner had detected "gases inflamables en el foco inicial, compatibles con el uso de acelerantes," that there were grounds to presume "intervención humana deliberada," and that the electrical-fault hypothesis initially under consideration had been ruled out. Soil samples went to the Argentine Federal Police laboratory; the Lago Puelo investigations brigade, the El Hoyo police station and the forensic cabinet worked the site. The ignition point was roughly 300 metres from a road in a remote area with no houses nearby. By February 27, 2026 four cases were open — one federal, over the Los Alerces national park fire, and three provincial under prosecutor general Carlos Díaz Mayer — with no one detained and no one charged. Díaz Mayer said the leading hypothesis was a dispute internal to the local community, and described the national-security framing about radicalised groups as "lo más alejado de la realidad." The account that circulated internationally, that Israeli soldiers disguised as tourists lit the fires, was rejected by the prosecutor leading the case as "un invento", with "la investigación no va por ese lado." The video most often attached to it, of a resident confronting two foreigners lighting a fire, was filmed in Los Glaciares National Park in Santa Cruz province, about 1,400 kilometres away; the person filming identified them as Israeli, which was never officially confirmed. The retired general César Milani and the activist Luis D'Elía separately accused Israeli tourists of igniting the blazes with Israel Defense Forces grenades, and AI-generated videos of supposed saboteurs circulated alongside the real footage.

sources.label: Ministerio Público Fiscal de la Provincia del Chubut — "Incendio en Puerto Patriada: Avanza la investigación de la Fiscalía de Lago Puelo," January 7, 2026, on the accelerant finding, the ruling out of an electrical cause, and the agencies working the site.

Cholila Online — "Incendios en Chubut: cuatro causas y ningún detenido," February 27, 2026, on the four open cases, the absence of charges, and prosecutor general Carlos Díaz Mayer on the community-dispute hypothesis.
sources.quote: lo más alejado de la realidad

sources.label: Chequeado (Argentine fact-checking organisation) — "Ni israelíes ni mapuches: qué se sabe sobre el origen de los incendios producidos en Chubut y los posibles responsables," on the Los Glaciares video's location in Santa Cruz and the prosecutor's rejection of the Israeli-tourist account.
sources.quote: existen elementos suficientes para presumir una intervención humana deliberada

sources.label: Middle East Forum — on the January 2026 accusations by César Milani and Luis D'Elía, the AI-generated videos, and prosecutors finding no evidence of organised arson.
sources.quote: Argentinian prosecutors found no evidence of organized arson.

notes: Upgraded from a fact-check-only citation to the Chubut MPF's own January 7, 2026 release as the primary. Both halves stand: the prosecutors do treat the ignition as deliberate and found accelerant, and the same prosecutors reject the Israeli-soldier account and name a local land dispute as the leading line. Charging status current to February 27, 2026, the most recent public state-of-play found; no arrest or imputación has been reported since. Díaz Mayer's 'lo más alejado de la realidad' was said of the radicalised-group framing pushed at national level, not of the Israeli-tourist claim, and is quoted that way.
